components.label: The holding mechanism where the thesis needs it (VASO-C010, VASO-C020, VASO-C077, VASO-C174, VASO-C143)
components.note: The latch is established in conduit arteries (VASO-E003 on VASO-C010) but not generic (VASO-E021 on VASO-C010). On VASO-C020, the report's audit finds no latch identified at any tender point (VASO-E016), no arteriole energetic cost has been measured (VASO-E019), and pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising phosphorylation (VASO-E020); the Doppler footprint (VASO-E027) is compatible with contracture. The competing fast non-vascular state (VASO-C077) and the perforator composite (VASO-C174) with its skin-territory write (VASO-C143) are anchor-only, the latter two in a source the ledger has not read.

components.label: The memory and contemplative attributions and their channels (VASO-C021, VASO-C022, VASO-C012, VASO-C013, VASO-C006)
components.note: The channels are real: vessels modulate neurons in rat brain (VASO-E005 on VASO-C012), slow breathing shifts autonomic balance globally (VASO-E009 on VASO-C013), attention regulates a peripheral bed at a chosen site (VASO-E008 on VASO-C006). None shows storage or readout. VASO-C021 is a hypothesis statement (VASO-E013, VASO-E038) that fails the write–store–read test (VASO-E017); VASO-C022 rests on a single uncited proponent assertion (VASO-E039) and awaits blinded coding.

researchPriority.reason: The decisive experiments are specified, cheap, and unrun: a time-locked imaging study of a single release, and a one-session repeat of an existing pressure-only compression protocol with breathing randomized. Either would move the case verdict in a way no further reading can, and the runners' protocol shows that the outcome measures already work within a single session.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on hypothesis statements alone: VASO-E013 states Johnson's three hypotheses as context, VASO-E038 relays the clinging identification second-hand, and VASO-E017 sets out why hysteresis is not yet memory — no admitted record shows a vascular state encoding a prior input, persisting after it, and biasing later neural output in a content-specific way. The channels the claim needs are evidenced on sibling claims (VASO-C012, VASO-C013, VASO-C006) but carry no storage.

treatment.plainLanguage: Tension in blood-vessel walls acts as a memory the mind uses — what Buddhists call clinging has a vascular address.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Nothing in the ledger tests it in either direction; the decisive animal experiment (VASO-R005) has not been run.
treatment.strongestObjection: A thermostat has hysteresis without an autobiography; vessels retaining tone contain information about their history but nothing shows that information is neurally read or content-specific.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An animal preparation in which different induced vascular states, with oxygenation clamped, produce reliably different later neural responses to identical stimulation after the initiating input has stopped.
A clean negative — vascular manipulation altering neural gain only through instantaneous perfusion — would collapse the claim to ordinary neurovascular physiology.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The two linchpins are graded absent by the report's audit (VASO-E016); the arteriole record shows maintained or rising phosphorylation, not a latch signature (VASO-E020), and no arteriole's holding cost has been measured (VASO-E019); the Doppler footprint near trigger points is supportive at zero diagnosticity because the authors list contracture compression as a co-equal cause (VASO-E027). VASO-E037 and VASO-E013 are the hypothesis stated by its proponents; VASO-E044 and VASO-E045 come from an unread source and are treated as absent. The mechanism is borrowed, not observed at a tender point, and where examined the compartment points the other way.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a small artery inside the muscle held shut cheaply by latched smooth muscle, starving its neighborhood, not damaged tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis the case grades; every observation rung is read against it.
treatment.strongestObjection: Pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles hold constriction by maintained activation, and every localized finding at trigger points — chemistry, Doppler, stiffness — is equally predicted by contracted fibre compressing its own bed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after stimulus withdrawal at falling phosphorylation and measured low energetic cost.
A palpated knot stiff on elastography, electrically active on EMG, and metabolically cold on FDG-PET.
Time-resolved imaging of a release with perfusion rising before stiffness falls, exceeding sham and pressure-only controls.
Against it: hot knots on PET, the non-latching motor-protein phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles, or release equal under held breath.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in a source (SRC-JHONG-2026A) the ledger has not been able to read and verify; no admitted evidence record bears on it. Featured because it is a genuinely different vascular mechanism with cheap tests, not because anything supports it.

treatment.plainLanguage: On the perforator picture, three things hold a knot at once — the vessel's tone, a collar of gelled hyaluronan, and the fascial sheet's tether — rather than one latch.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If tender points sit on perforators and release by hydrodissection without breath, this account displaces the latch; if they do not, it dies in an afternoon.
treatment.strongestObjection: The stiff regions blinded sonographers report lie inside the muscle, not in the fascia under the skin, and no perforator has ever been measured at a tender point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded tender points coinciding with pencil-Doppler-mapped perforators above chance.
A knot released by ultrasound-guided saline hydrodissection at its perforator with no breath and no pressure.
Against it: coincidence at chance, or saline around the vessel doing nothing.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The only record in either direction is VASO-E039, the founding essay's uncited assertion that traditional maps place knots along the midline and limbs, with no coding rule or chance baseline. No blinded anatomical coding exists; post-hoc matching cannot be excluded.

treatment.plainLanguage: Tibetan, Indian and Chinese maps of bodily knots and channels are first-person records of the same tension system, felt from inside.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Even a genuine alignment with vascular geography would not show that anything latches or clenches; it would show the maps are empirical documents.
treatment.strongestObjection: Any rich body map can be matched to any rich anatomy after the fact; without preregistered coding the convergence is pattern-matching.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Preregistered blinded coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi locations aligning with vascular branch points, sympathetic chains or fascial perforation sites better than chance.
Coding at chance would retire the convergence argument.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hai and Murphy's kinetic model reproduces sustained stress at low phosphorylation in vascular smooth muscle (VASO-E003, strong). VASO-E021 qualifies the generality: latch behaviour was present in a parent artery and absent one branch order downstream, so the capability is real but vessel-type-dependent. VASO-E034 is a restatement that overstates the model (low, not zero, activation).

treatment.plainLanguage: Smooth muscle in vessel walls can hold tension cheaply after the signal that started it has faded — the latch.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Textbook physiology that every account accepts; it decides nothing unless the latch is shown in the vessels a knot would need.
treatment.strongestObjection: Demonstrated in conduit arteries over minutes to hours; not generic across vascular smooth muscle and never followed into the microcirculation.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A paired-caliber study finding the non-latching motor-protein phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles would confine the capability to vessels irrelevant to knots.
Latch-competent arterioles with a stimulus-withdrawal phase would extend it to where the thesis needs it.

claimAssessments.reasoning: An inference graded on physiological priors: remodeling takes days to weeks, so a seconds-scale objective release would be a state change. The ledger holds the argument as stated (VASO-E035, weak) and a pilot in which imaged measures moved over visits after needling (VASO-E030, context). The premise — an objective local change within seconds — has never been measured; the conditional is sound, its antecedent unestablished.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a knot really lets go in seconds, whatever let go was something the body was doing, not scar tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Separates state from scar, which all three live accounts accept; it does not separate a vessel from guarding or densification.
treatment.strongestObjection: 'State' is a bigger tent than 'vascular': sustained motor guarding and fascial densification are states too, and the seconds-scale objective release the premise needs has not been filmed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved elastography showing a stiffness step within seconds of a felt release, at palpated but not sham sites.
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition would remove the antecedent.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone (the founding essay's statement of the Stecco group's densification concept); no admitted evidence record, and the primary literature on hyaluronan viscosity and its timescale has not been retrieved.

treatment.plainLanguage: The gel between fascial layers can thicken and then thin again under pressure, movement and warmth — a fast, non-vascular kind of state.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If densification reverses within seconds under pressure, the knot can be a state without being a vessel and pressure alone should work; if it takes hours, a seconds-scale release needs a vascular or neural account.
treatment.strongestObjection: No study in the ledger reports the timescale of densification reversal, and the concept has not been shown to constitute any painful trigger point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retrieved primary data giving the timescale of hyaluronan viscosity change under load and warmth.
Imaging of a release showing stiffness dropping with no perfusion change.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The hypothesis paper (VASO-E004, context) proposes the read path; the 2024 Science demonstration (VASO-E005, strong) shows blood-pressure pulsations modulating central neurons via mechanosensitive channels in rat preparations and awake animals. This is instantaneous modulation in brain, not storage, and not the human periphery.

treatment.plainLanguage: Blood vessels can influence what nearby neurons do, not just feed them.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Establishes a channel every account can accommodate; it says nothing about knots, storage or content.
treatment.strongestObjection: Rat brain, fast mechanosensation; the extension to peripheral sensory endings beside knot-scale vessels is argument, not measurement.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Demonstration of vascular mechanical modulation of peripheral sensory afferents at a tender point.
History-dependent neural readout under clamped oxygenation (VASO-R005).

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review of slow-breathing studies in healthy humans documents reproducible rises in heart-rate variability and respiratory sinus arrhythmia (VASO-E009, strong); VASO-E036 is an uncited restatement. The evidence is global and cardiac, with no tender-point measurement.

treatment.plainLanguage: Breathing slowly, with long exhales, reliably shifts the body toward its rest-and-digest setting.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A global shift measured on the heart is exactly what the conventional account also invokes; local, site-specific unlatching is the untested addition.
treatment.strongestObjection: Measured in people with no tender point in the study; nothing here links the shift to any local tissue event.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A local stiffness or perfusion change time-locked to the exhale at a knot and not at sham sites.
Pressure during an inhale-and-hold blocking clearance that free breathing permits.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Systematic review finds manual examination not shown reliable or valid, with no reference standard (VASO-E011, strong); the peer-reviewed construct critique (VASO-E010); proponent-side concessions that palpation is subjective (VASO-E029) and that there is no gold standard and inter-observer variability cannot be trained away (VASO-E078, VASO-E079), with imaging confirming 71.5% of palpated spots (VASO-E081; VASO-E080 context). The critique drew a rebuttal; the exchange is the state of the debate.

treatment.plainLanguage: Examiners cannot reliably agree on where trigger points are, there is no agreed test for one, and the peer-reviewed literature disputes the concept.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Softens the observation base for every account equally; it does not favor any mechanism, but it means every decisive study must localize by instrument before it measures.
treatment.strongestObjection: The critique targets the manual exam and the classic taut-band construct, not the instrumented abnormalities blinded sonographers report at palpated sites.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A reliability study showing high inter-examiner agreement against an imaging reference standard.
A census with pain-free controls in which instrumented stiffness and flow fail to pick out palpated spots would strengthen the critique.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Croft 1994 supplies the first population record: two people reporting no pain had eleven or more tender points at the eighteen fixed sites (VASO-E082, weak), in a pain-selected sample (VASO-E083 context). VASO-E028 is a second-hand 1986 prevalence estimate for a pain syndrome, VASO-E015 is proponent testimony, VASO-E018 is scanner context, and VASO-E012 qualifies: the reproducibility of the spots is itself disputed.

treatment.plainLanguage: Small, very tender spots are common in ordinary people's muscles.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: All accounts accept that people have tender spots; the claim frames the phenomenon without choosing between mechanisms.
treatment.strongestObjection: No census exists; the one instrumented glimpse tested fixed sites in a pain-selected sample, and the examiners' reliability is unproven.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A knot census with blinded palpation, algometry and imaging across the age span, including pain-free controls.
A community survey with unselected sampling reporting count distributions.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hubbard and Berkoff found sustained activity in the nidus and none in adjacent non-tender fibres (VASO-E001); Simons 2002 qualifies exclusivity — endplate noise at 4 of 11 non-tender endplate-zone sites, none off the zone (VASO-E031). The claim is stated as the resulting prevalence gradient. VASO-E043 is a derivative restatement; VASO-E052 (equine EMG) is context from an unread source.

treatment.plainLanguage: Trigger points hum electrically more often than quiet spots in the same nerve-supply zone, and never where there is no such zone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Shows the knot is electrically maintained — state, not scar — but the signature is skeletal endplate electrophysiology and says nothing about vessels.
treatment.strongestObjection: The signature tracks the endplate zone first; the silent control sites of 1993 may simply have lain off the zone.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Needle EMG at trigger points against matched endplate-zone controls with modern instrumentation.
Sympathetic blockade quieting the nidus (VASO-R009) would tie it to autonomic drive without yet making it vascular.

claimAssessments.reasoning: One study of fourteen subjects from the Hubbard lineage (VASO-E002, moderate) found mental arithmetic raised trigger-point activity while control sites stayed comparatively quiet; VASO-E033 restates it. The control needle was not placed in a matched endplate-zone site, so selection of the trigger point versus any endplate zone is open; never replicated; no vascular measurement.

treatment.plainLanguage: Doing sums in your head turns up the electrical activity inside a trigger point but not in nearby muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The write half of any storage account — but stress-sensitive endplates, an arteriole write and a skin-territory write all predict it, and the needle cannot tell them apart.
treatment.strongestObjection: Without a matched endplate-zone control the site-selectivity is unproven, and the recorded signal is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A repeat with an electrically located endplate-zone control: selective rise at the trigger point restores addressability; equal rise relocates the effect to stress-sensitive endplates.
A skin-perfusion fall over the point and not over control skin during the stressor.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in a source (SRC-JHONG-2026A) the ledger has not read; no admitted evidence record. It is the perforator account's reading of the stressor result on VASO-C003, and it makes a distinct, cheap prediction.

treatment.plainLanguage: The stressor's effect on a trigger point is the brain narrowing skin vessels in one patch, the way it blushes or blanches a patch.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A skin-perfusion camera during mental arithmetic would separate this from stress-sensitive endplates and from an intramuscular write.
treatment.strongestObjection: The 1994 signal was recorded by a needle in muscle; no skin perfusion was measured, and blushing is a face-and-neck phenomenon, not a millimetre-scale one.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Laser speckle imaging showing a localized perfusion fall over the tender point and not over control skin during a mental stressor.
Perfusion unchanged or global would remove the reading.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Supported only by first-person and practitioner testimony from the hypothesis's proponent (VASO-E014, weak), in an essay whose text was AI-generated; consistent with practitioner lore, contradicted by no record, measured by no one. Credible as an experience; expectation and attention cannot be excluded.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press on a knot and breathe out slowly, and within seconds something feels like it lets go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: As a felt event it decides nothing: every account predicts that people feel releases. Only an objective local correlate would make it diagnostic.
treatment.strongestObjection: A felt release is exactly what expectation riding on global relaxation would produce, and nothing in the tissue has been shown to change.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-locked imaging showing a local stiffness or perfusion transition at each button press, exceeding sham and pressure-only controls.
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition would leave the claim true as testimony and empty as mechanism.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor (proponent testimony) with one admitted record, VASO-E067 (direction context), which establishes that a published pressure-only protocol carried no breathing instruction, recording or manipulation — and nothing more. What that protocol achieved is admitted on VASO-C005, not here, and its endpoint was minutes-scale sonographic disappearance, not a felt release timed to an exhale; breathing was uncontrolled, so a spontaneous exhale under pressure cannot be excluded.

treatment.plainLanguage: Pressing on a knot without the breath does not release it — you need both keys.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If pressure alone suffices, the cleanest argument that the releasing element answers to autonomic state falls; if held breath blocks release, breath-gating is real and both vascular accounts gain.
treatment.strongestObjection: A pressure-only protocol in runners cleared most imaged trigger points within one session with nobody told how to breathe.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: The runners' protocol repeated with breathing randomized: equal clearance under inhale-and-hold refutes the claim; blocked clearance under held breath supports it.
Release by saline hydrodissection with no breath would refute necessity.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone (the founding essay's stated prediction); no admitted evidence record. No study in the ledger has observed the order of perfusion and stiffness change at a release — the runners' study performed no Doppler and archived no cine loops.

treatment.plainLanguage: When a knot releases with the breath, blood comes back first and the tissue softens second.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The one timing prediction the vascular accounts make and their rivals do not; either ordering would be decisive.
treatment.strongestObjection: It is a prediction with no measurement behind it in any tissue; stiffness leading or simultaneous change would fit guarding or densification.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved Doppler and elastography across release events showing perfusion leading stiffness.
Stiffness leading, or the two simultaneous, or no perfusion change at all.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Group-level differences are supported on three axes: biochemistry (VASO-E006), stiffness by blinded vibration sonoelastography with ROC separation of site classes (VASO-E087, VASO-E090, VASO-E091, VASO-E094, VASO-E096, VASO-E099) and Doppler pulsatility (VASO-E022), with a second-hand systematic review (VASO-E007). The same source qualifies: no pain-free controls (VASO-E026), flow indices that cannot classify sites (VASO-E025), sites selected by palpation, one vibration frequency, one NIH lineage. Landfald's calf differences are active against latent with no control tissue (VASO-E069, VASO-E071, VASO-E072 context; VASO-E070 qualifies). VASO-E042, VASO-E050 and VASO-E051 are essay restatements, the last two from an unread source.

treatment.plainLanguage: Where an examiner finds a trigger point, instruments find tissue that is more acidic, stiffer, and has somewhat different local blood flow than its surroundings.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Something is there — but contracted fibre compressing its own bed predicts the chemistry, the stiffness and the Doppler as readily as a throttled vessel does.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every comparison sits inside symptomatic muscle at palpation-selected sites, the vascular signature is partial, and none of it says what the stiff tissue is.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A census with pain-free controls and instrument-fixed sites in which stiffness and flow measures fail to pick out palpated spots.
Time-resolved imaging showing what changes first when a point releases.

claimAssessments.reasoning: One laboratory's preregistered within-subject experiments in 57 volunteers (VASO-E008, strong) found ~1.5-fold smaller and faster-resolving histamine responses under inward attention with no arousal difference. VASO-E041 relays the authors' caveat: a vagal immune route over tens of minutes, in skin the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate. Single lab, very recent.

treatment.plainLanguage: Paying attention to an inflamed patch of skin makes the inflammation smaller and shorter-lived, without any change in stress arousal.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that cognition can write to a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site; it concerns neither knots, smooth muscle nor seconds.
treatment.strongestObjection: Immune regulation over twenty minutes by a vagal route is a different channel from seconds-scale unlatching of a vessel.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication in a second laboratory.
Extension of the paradigm to stiffness or perfusion at a tender point.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Reported directly by the primary (VASO-E022): median pulsatility index 8.3 near active sites against 3.0 near normal sites, blinded sonographers. Qualified by VASO-E026: no pain-free controls, 'normal' sites in symptomatic muscle. The vessels are conduit-scale and the index could not classify individual sites.

treatment.plainLanguage: Arteries near active trigger points show sharper surge-and-fall of blood flow with each heartbeat than arteries near normal spots in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Compatible with distal constriction, contracture compressing the bed, inflammation or transducer pressure — the authors list all four.
treatment.strongestObjection: The index varied so widely it could not classify any site, and the vessels interrogated are far larger than the microvessels a latch account needs.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A Doppler census with pain-free controls.
Microvascular Doppler at knot depth during a release.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Reported directly by the primary (VASO-E022): retrograde diastolic flow at 15 of 49 palpably normal sites (31%), against 55% of active sites. VASO-E026 qualifies: the normal sites were five centimetres from a trigger point in symptomatic muscle, so this may be baseline or spillover.

treatment.plainLanguage: Backward flow between heartbeats also shows up near almost a third of palpably normal spots in muscles that have trigger points elsewhere.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Turns the Doppler waveform from a marker of a knot into a gradient across symptomatic muscle, which weakens the 'footprint of something clenched' reading.
treatment.strongestObjection: Without pain-free controls the 31% cannot be called either a baseline rate or spillover from neighbouring points.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retrograde flow rates in pain-free muscle.
A gradient of retrograde flow with distance from the nearest palpated point.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The paper's own results report the figures (VASO-E087 gives the active 0.57 ± 0.20 cm²; VASO-E089 the latent 0.36 ± 0.16 cm²), with the active-over-latent significance and ROC separation as context (VASO-E093, VASO-E095). Sonographers were blinded to clinical status. One laboratory, one vibration frequency from an off-the-shelf massager, sites selected by palpation, same NIH lineage as the biochemistry; the calf active/latent area difference (VASO-E085) is context from another muscle and method, not a replication.

treatment.plainLanguage: On stiffness imaging, the stiff region at a spontaneously painful trigger point is larger than at one that hurts only when pressed.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A graded stiff region tracks symptom severity under guarding as readily as under a throttled vessel; it establishes that the imaging sees something, not what.
treatment.strongestObjection: The measured contrast presupposes the palpated classification, and the technique's frequency-independence and shear elasticity were not established.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Replication with shear-wave elastography in a second laboratory with instrument-fixed sites.
A census with pain-free controls in which the gradient disappears.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Reported directly in the paper's results: palpably normal sites 0.17 ± 0.22 cm² with the across-class difference at P < .01 (VASO-E090), active and latent significantly larger than normal (VASO-E091), area an excellent classifier of active versus normal at AUC 0.9 (VASO-E096) and a fair classifier of latent versus normal at AUC 0.79 (VASO-E098); VASO-E095 is ROC context. Same design limits as VASO-C182: blinded sonographers, one laboratory, palpation-selected sites, 'normal' sites in symptomatic muscle.

treatment.plainLanguage: Both kinds of trigger point show a larger stiff region on imaging than palpably normal spots in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Confirms the palpated spot is instrumentally distinct from its surroundings; every account accepts that and none is chosen by it.
treatment.strongestObjection: The 'normal' sites lie in symptomatic muscle a few centimetres from a trigger point, so the contrast is within patients, not against health.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Stiff-area measurements at matched sites in pain-free subjects.
Failure of the contrast when sites are fixed by instrument rather than thumb.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Reported in the abstract of Simons, Hong and Simons 2002 (VASO-E032): endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites against eleven of eleven trigger-point sites. Small, nonrandomized, unblinded, proponent authors; abstract only.

treatment.plainLanguage: The electrical hum also occurs at some non-tender spots, provided they lie in the muscle's nerve-supply zone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Places the signature in the endplate zone first and the trigger point second — the conventional skeletal-endplate reading — and exposes the missing matched control in the stressor experiment.
treatment.strongestObjection: Ten subjects, unblinded; the prevalence gradient (11/11 versus 4/11) still favors the trigger point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded replication with per-site amplitudes.
A matched endplate-zone control rising under mental arithmetic.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Reported in the same abstract (VASO-E032): endplate noise did not occur at taut-band sites outside an endplate zone (P = 0.000034). Same design limits — small, unblinded, abstract only.

treatment.plainLanguage: Tight bands that lie outside the nerve-supply zone produce no electrical hum.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Ties the signature to the endplate zone rather than to tautness or tenderness as such; a vessel account must explain why a throttled bed off the zone is silent.
treatment.strongestObjection: Taut bands themselves are palpation-defined, and the study did not blind the needle placement.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Spontaneous activity recorded at off-zone taut bands under blinded placement.
Vascular measurements at off-zone taut bands showing the same flow abnormality as on-zone points.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Reported directly by the primary (VASO-E024): no differences in resistivity index between active, latent and normal sites, with the pulsatility index a poor classifier because of variance. Within-patient comparison in symptomatic subjects.

treatment.plainLanguage: A second measure of downstream blood-flow resistance shows no difference at all between trigger points and normal spots.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A null on the vascular axis: the flow signature at trigger points is partial, not categorical, which weakens any reading of the Doppler as a marker.
treatment.strongestObjection: The authors attribute the similarity partly to proximity of 'normal' sites to trigger points, so the null may reflect the design rather than the tissue.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Resistivity index differences against pain-free controls.
Microvascular rather than conduit-scale Doppler at the point itself.
